title: Parashurama arrives
introduction: Parashu Rama confronts the wedding party that is returning to Ayodhya from Mithila. On his very entry, the atmosphere becomes pell-mell and a whirlwind ensues. Expecting some problem from this Parashu Rama, the sages like Vashishta and others starts to receive him in a peaceable manner. Not caring anyone around Parashu Rama starts a dialogue with Dasharatha Rama.
closing: इति वाल्मीकिरामायणे आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे चतुःसप्ततितमः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 74th chapter in Bala Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
अथ रात्र्यां व्यतीतायां विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः |
आपृच्छ्य तौ च राजानौ जगामोत्तरपर्वतम्
verses.iast:
atha rātryām vyatītāyām viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ |
āpṛṣṭvā tau ca rājānau jagāma uttara parvatam
verses.translation: When that night is elapsing into the wee hours of next day, then the eminent-saint Vishvamitra on asking for the leave of absence from those kings, Dasharatha and Janaka, and from both Rama and Lakshmana, he set out to northern mountains, namely Himalayas.

verses.devanagari:
विश्वामित्रो गते राजा वैदेहं मिथिलाधिपम् |
आपृष्ट्वैव जगामाशु राजा दशरथः पुरीम्
verses.iast:
viśvāmitro gate rājā vaideham mithilā adhipam |
āpṛṣṭva iva jagāma āśu rājā daśarathaḥ purīm
verses.translation: When Vishvamitra departed that ruler to the delight of people, namely Dasharatha, on asking leave of absence with king Janaka who outvies bodily affairs, promptly set forth for the city of Ayodhya.

glosses.meaning: the ruler to the delight of people, Dasharatha
one who outvies bodily affairs - Janaka
promptly, for city Ayodhya, set forth.

verses.devanagari:
अथ राजा विदेहानां ददौ कन्याधनं बहु |
गवां शतसहस्राणि बहूनि मिथिलेश्वरः
कंबलानां च मुख्यानां क्षौमान् कोट्यंबराणि च |
हस्त्यश्वरथपादातं दिव्यरूपं स्वलंकृतम्
ददौ कन्याशतं तासां दासीदासमनुत्तमम् |
verses.iast:
atha rājā videhānām dadau kanyā dhanam bahu |
gavām śata sahasrāṇi bahūni mithileśvaraḥ
kambalānām ca mukhyānām kṣaumān koṭi ambarāṇi ca |
hasti aśva ratha pādātam divya rūpam svalaṅkṛtam
dadau kanyā śatam tāsām dāsī dāsam anuttamam |
verses.translation: Then that king Janaka of Mithila, the one from Videha lineage, gave innumerable patrimonial riches. He has also given umpteen number of cows, millions of excellent shawls and silk dresses, and elephants, horses, chariots, foot soldiers, besides hundreds of highly decorated girls, divine in their mien, as unexcelled chambermaids and handmaidens to the brides.

glosses.meaning: hundred, thousands [millions of,] excellent ones, shawls, also

verses.devanagari:
हिरण्यस्य सुवर्णस्य मुक्तानां विद्रुमस्य च
ददौ राजा सुसंहृष्टः कन्याधनमनुत्तमम् |
verses.iast:
hiraṇyasya suvarṇasya muktānām vidrumasya ca
dadau rājā susaṃhṛṣṭaḥ kanyā dhanam anuttamam |
verses.translation: King Janaka gave beau idéal bridal riches in gold, silver, pearls and corals even, for he is very highly gladdened as Seetha's marriage came true.

verses.devanagari:
दत्त्वा बहुविधं राजा समनुज्ञाप्य पार्थिवम्
प्रविवेश स्वनिलयं मिथिलां मिथिलेश्वरः |
verses.iast:
dattvā bahu vidham rājā samanujñāpya pārthivam
praviveśa sva nilayam mithilām mithileśvaraḥ |
verses.translation: Having given many kinds of bridal gifts and having accompanied his daughters for a distance, then having received a bid adieu from Dasharatha, that sovereign of Mithila, Janaka, re-entered is own palace in Mithila.
notes: It is customary to follow the wedding party up to the outskirts of village or town. In the meantime, there will be two or three hugs of mother and the bride, shedding two or three litres of tears, while the father of the bride secretly wipes his own moist eyes, and the like. Because, this despatch of the bride is considered as another life to her, for she cannot come to her father's house as and when she wants. Even if she comes, she has to return to her husband's place at some point of time, because from now onward 'that' house has become 'her' house. In this particular case of Seetha, she does not come to Mithila after this episode and even when Rama abandons her she goes into the womb of her mother, Mother Earth, but not to Mithila. So let us leave Janaka and his queen as they have the satisfaction in marrying their daughter, whose marriage itself is problematical so far, and when that has happened, now some sort of dissatisfaction has cropped up, in leaving her off with some forest ranger, called Rama.

glosses.meaning: on making Dasharatha to bid adieu

verses.devanagari:
राजाप्ययोध्याधिपतिः सह पुत्रैर्महात्मभिः
ऋषीन् सर्वान् पुरस्कृत्य जगाम सबलानुगः |
verses.iast:
rājā api ayodhyā adhipatiḥ saha putraiḥ mahātmabhiḥ
ṛṣīn sarvān puraskṛtya jagāma sa bala anugaḥ |
verses.translation: Even the king Dasharatha, the sovereign of Ayodhya proceeded with his noble-souled sons, keeping all the sages in the fore, while his forces followed him.

glosses.meaning: Ayodhya's, sovereign, king Dasharatha, even mahaa aatmabhiH putraiH saha = with noble-souled, sons, along with

verses.devanagari:
गच्छन्तं तु नरव्याघ्रं सर्षिसंघं सराघवम्
घोरास्तु पक्षिणो वाचो व्याहरन्ति समंततः |
verses.iast:
gacchantam tu naravyāghram sa ṛṣi saṅgham sa rāghavam
ghorāḥ tu pakṣiṇo vāco vyāharanti samantataḥ |
verses.translation: But while going with the assemblages of sages and with young Raghava-s, namely Rama, Lakshmana, Bharata, Shatrughna, the sky-bound birds started to screech with startling voice from all around facing that tigerly-man Dasharatha.

glosses.meaning: with [young] Raghava-s - Rama, Lakshmana, Bharata, Shatrughna
birds, with horrible, voice, started to screech.

verses.devanagari:
भौमाश्चैव मृगाः सर्वे गच्छन्ति स्म प्रदक्षिणम्
तान् दृष्ट्वा राजशार्दूलो वसिष्ठं पर्यपृच्छत |
verses.iast:
bhaumāḥ caiva mṛgāḥ sarve gacchanti sma pradakṣiṇam
tān dṛṣṭvā rāja śārdūlo vasiṣṭham paryapṛcchata |
verses.translation: Also thus, all of the earth bound animals are going his leftward, and on seeing this, albeit he is a tigerly king he is perplexed, and particularly asked Vashishta.

verses.devanagari:
असौम्याः पक्षिणो घोरा मृगाश्चापि प्रदक्षिणाः
किमिदं हृदयोत्कंपि मनो मम विषीदति |
verses.iast:
asauṃyāḥ pakṣiṇo ghorā mṛgāḥ ca api pradakṣiṇāḥ
kim idam hṛdaya utkampi mano mama viṣīdati |
verses.translation: "Unpropitious is the starling voicing of birds, whereby my heart is throbbing down... and propitious is the leftward going of the animals, thereby my heart is throbbing up... why so?"

glosses.meaning: heart, to up, beating [with one's heart in one's mouth, throbbing up]

verses.devanagari:
राज्ञो दशरथस्यैतत् श्रुत्वा वाक्यं महानृषिः
उवाच मधुरां वाणीं श्रूयतामस्य यत्फलम् |
verses.iast:
rājño daśarathasya etat śrutvā vākyam mahān ṛṣiḥ
uvāca madhurām vāṇīm śrūyatām asya yat phalam |
verses.translation: On hearing all that is said by king Dasharatha, the instinctual sage Vashishta said this sentence in a soothing voice, "I will tell apart the result of these auguries...

glosses.meaning: in a soothing, voice, [this] sentence, said

verses.devanagari:
उपस्थितं भयं घोरं दिव्यं पक्षिमुखाच्च्युतम्
मृगाः प्रशमयन्त्येते संतापः त्यज्यतामयम् |
verses.iast:
upasthitam bhayam ghoram divyam pakṣi mukhāt cyutam
mṛgāḥ praśamayanti ete santāpaḥ tyajyatām ayam |
verses.translation: "The shrieks voiced by the birds are foretokening the forthcoming providential and perilous trepidation, but the behaviour of these animals is betokening it as mitigable... hence, let this consternation be forsaken...

glosses.meaning: bird's, from mouths, fallen [shrieks voiced, foretokening]

verses.devanagari:
तेषां संवदतां तत्र वायुः प्रादुर्बभूव ह
कंपयन् मेदिनीं सर्वां पातयंश्च महाद्रुमान् |
verses.iast:
teṣām saṃvadatām tatra vāyuḥ prādur babhūva ha
kampayan medinīm sarvām pātayan ca mahān drumān |
verses.translation: While they are discussing among themselves, a whirlwind started to whirligig there, as though to shake the earth and shatter all gigantic trees.

verses.devanagari:
तमसा संवृतः सूर्यः सर्वे न वेदिषुर्दिशः
भस्मना चावृतं सर्वं सम्मूढमिव तद्बलम् |
verses.iast:
tamasā saṃvṛtaḥ sūryaḥ sarve na vediṣur diśaḥ
bhasmanā ca āvṛtam sarvam sammūḍham iva tat balam |
verses.translation: Murkiness enshrouded the sun, thus everyone is unaware of quarters, a sandstorm enwrapped that army, by which it has become as though ensorcelled.

verses.devanagari:
वसिष्ठ ऋषयचान्ये राजा च ससुतस्तदा
ससंज्ञा इव तत्रासन् सर्वमन्यद्विचेतनम् |
verses.iast:
vasiṣṭha ṛṣayaḥ ca anye rājā ca sasutaḥ tadā
sa saṃjñā iva tatra āsan sarvam anyat vicetanam |
verses.translation: Then Vashishta and the other sages, the king Dasharatha along with his sons remained there with animation, and everything and every other one available there has become inanimate.

glosses.meaning: every other one, everything, is without, animation.

verses.devanagari:
तस्मिंस्तमसि घोरे तु भस्मच्छन्नेव सा चमूः
ददर्श भीमसंकाशं जटामण्डलधारिणम् |
भार्गवं जामदग्न्यं तं राजा राजविमर्दनम्
कैलासमिव दुर्धर्षं कालाग्निमिव दुःसहम् |
ज्वलंतमिव तेजोभिः दुर्निरीक्ष्यं पृथग्जनैः
स्कन्धे चासज्य परशुं धनुर्विद्युद्गणोपमम् |
प्रगृह्य शरमुग्रं च त्रिपुरघ्नं यथा शिवम्
verses.iast:
tasmin tamasi ghore tu bhasma channa iva sā camūḥ
dadarśa bhīma saṅkāśam jaṭā maṇḍala dhāriṇam |
bhārgavam jamadagne ayam rājā rāja vimardanam
kailāsam iva durdharṣam kāla agnim iva duḥsaham |
jvalantam iva tejobhiḥ dur nirīkṣyam pṛthak janaiḥ
skandhe ca āsajya paraśum dhanuḥ vidyut gaṇa upamam |
pragṛhya śaram ugram ca tri pura ghnam yathā śivam
verses.translation: In that catastrophic darkness, that sand-muffled military of king Dasharatha has seen the son of Sage Jamadagni, namely Bhaargava Rama, the subjugator of kings of kings. He appeared calamitous in his look by wearing tufty matted and unruly head-hair, an unassailable one like Mt. Kailash, an unbearable one like the Epoch-End-Fire, irradiant with his own radiance, hence imperceivable for commoners, and such as he is, he clinched an axe on his right shoulder and clasped a bow in his left hand, that in simile is like a congeries of electroluminescence, and handling an arrow which is as if ready to electrocute, and he vied in his overall look with the devastator of triple cities, namely God Shiva.

glosses.meaning: by ashes [sand,] muffled up, as though
he [who is,] king, of kings, subjugator of
with his own radiance, irradiant, like
by common, people, one impossible, to gaze at
electric discharges, groups, in simile to
triple, cities, devastator, Shiva, as with
him, sage Jamadagni's, Bhaargava, they all have seen.

verses.devanagari:
तं दृष्ट्वा भीमसंकाशं ज्वलंतमिव पावकम् |
वसिष्ठप्रमुखा विप्रा जपहोमपरायणाः
संगता मुनयः सर्वे संजजल्पुरथो मिथः |
verses.iast:
tam dṛṣṭvā bhīma saṅkāśam jvalantam iva pāvakam |
vasiṣṭha pramukhā viprā japa homa parāyaṇāḥ
saṅgatā munayaḥ sarve sañjajalpuḥ atho mithaḥ |
verses.translation: On seeing him who is perilous in his propensity and flaming like the Ritual-fire, Vashishta and the other prominent Brahman-s who are the practisers of meditation and fire-oblations have come together and started to susurrate, up and down.

glosses.meaning: all of the, sages, coming together

verses.devanagari:
कच्चित् पितृवधामर्षी क्षत्र ं नोत्सादयिष्यति
पूर्वं क्षत्रवधं कृत्वा गतमन्युर्गतज्वरः |
क्षत्रस्योत्सादनं भूयो न खल्वस्य चिकीर्षितम्
verses.iast:
kaccit pitṛ vadha amarṣī kṣatram na utsādayiṣyati
pūrvam kṣatra vadham kṛtvā gata manyuḥ gata jvaraḥ |
kṣatrasya utsādanam bhūyo na khalu asya cikīrṣitam
verses.translation: "Will he eradicate the race of Kshatriya-s even now as he was once envenomed by the murder of his father, or what... abated is his anger and alleviated is his frenzy previously when he eliminated Kshatriya-s... but is he really intending to eliminate Kshatriya-s once again, or what?" Thus, those Brahmans talked among themselves.
notes: An account of Parashu Rama's elimination of Kshatriya clans is given in endnote.

glosses.meaning: Kshatriya race, not, going to eradicate [now,] will he be - or what

verses.devanagari:
एवमुक्त्वार्घ्यमादाय भार्गवं भीमदर्शनम् |
ऋषयो राम रामेति मधुरं वाक्यमब्रुवन्
verses.iast:
evam uktvā arghyam ādāya bhārgavam bhīma darśanam |
ṛṣayo rāma rāma iti madhuram vākyam abruvan
verses.translation: After their susurrus the sages have approached him, who in his very look is like a visitation, with oblational water and addressed him with benign words of greeting like, "oh, Rama, oh, Bhaargava Rama..."

glosses.meaning: a visitation, in his look, towards Bhaargava Rama
thus, sweetly [benignly,] sentence [lines of greetings,] while speaking - they approached.

verses.devanagari:
प्रतिगृह्य तु तां पूजामृषिदत्तां प्रतापवान् |
रामं दाशरथिं रामो जामदग्न्योऽभ्यभाषत
verses.iast:
pratigṛhya tu tām pūjām ṛṣi dattām pratāpavān |
rāmam dāśarathim rāmo jāmadag.hnyo abhyabhāṣata
verses.translation: On receiving the deference paid by the sage Vashishta, that inexorable Rama of Jamadagni started to talk to Rama of Dasharatha.

glosses.meaning: of Dasharatha, to Rama, started to talk.
